pr_title: gh-102828: add onexc arg to shutil.rmtree. Deprecate onerror.
pr_body:
onexc expects an exception instead of exc_info.  This is part of the larger effort to move on from exc_info.

Fixes #102828.

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-102828 -->
* Issue: gh-102828

Ignore my experiment with the 1st buildbot report.

Hey, why does `onexc` accept three arguments (function, path, exc) rather than just the exception?

If it accepted only one argument, then:

1. It would match the `onerror` argument to `os.walk()` and `os.fwalk()`
2. Users could still get the file path that failed via `exc.filename`
3. Users could still print the exception/traceback to display exactly what failed

The only thing lost would be the `function` value, which seems like an unreasonably detailed insight into the internals of `rmtree()`. In fact, `rmtree()` already bends the truth about the function that actually failed - for example `os.path.islink` is given if we fail a junction check on Windows. And no internal code looks at the value of `function`.

> Hey, why does `onexc` accept three arguments (function, path, exc) rather than just the exception?

Because that's what onerror did. This PR was just about replacing exc_info by exc. Feel free to suggest additional changes in a separate issue.

issue_context.title: add option for error callback of to shutil.rmtree to accept exception rather than exc_info
issue_context.body:
shutil.rmtree accepts as ``onerror`` a callback to should expect an exc_info tuple. To move off this, I will add a new kwarg "onexc" which should expect just an exception object. ``onerror``  will continue to work for now, but be deprecated.

comments: I think it is too early to deprecate `onerror`. It only creates inconvenience for code that should support multiple Python versions. Opened #112645 for this.

What is the urgency in removing the 'onerror' parameter? A concern about shutil.rmtree performance of accepting both arguments? Or is it just part of the core-python lemming-suicide pact to drive users away by making python as consistently self-incompatible as possible?

> What is the urgency in removing the 'onerror' parameter? 

Nobody indicated any urgency. You made that up just so you can entertain us with your witty insult.

review_comments: Do you want to add the deprecation warning already?

Personally I would add the warning already, but I'm not sure if there's a general deprecation policy. I took a look at the devguide but it doesn't seem to mention any. For this it's probably better to ask / CC someone else.
Ok, we can decide on that later.  We can add the deprecation warning separately.

I think the concern is that people who would like to continue supporting 3.10 and 3.11 will be harassed by a deprecation warning on 3.12 while they do that. So it might be nicer to let them wait with the upgrade until 3.10 is out of the way.
It's fine with me. I'm gonna approve the PR since overall LGTM.
